A barrow mound shaped deliberately into a coiled dragon form, the ridge of the tail and the swell of the haunches legible in the landscape only from above, gorse growing along the spine-ridge in a continuous dark stripe.

A dragon horn spiraling from a hilltop like a great ivory tower, wider at the base than a cottage, its surface grooved in a continuous helical channel that funnels wind into a low moan audible across the surrounding valley.

An ancient dragon nest of fused branches, bone shards, and compressed ash as broad as an amphitheater and half as deep, the inner bowl glazed smooth by heat long past, the outer rim encrusted with the petrified remains of prey.

A mummified dragon wing draped over the collapsed walls of a fortress ruin, the leathery membrane still largely intact and opaque, its span covering three towers, the leading edge bone pressing through dried skin like fingers through a worn glove.

A dragon breastbone keel rising from the moor like a ship's upturned prow, taller than any standing tower in the lowlands, its ventral surface ribbed with attachment ridges for flight muscles whose power can only be imagined against that scale.

A skull-crowned standing-stone ring on the chalk downs, each megalith topped with a carved dragon-skull motif, but at the circle's center rests a genuine skull fragment the size of a longhouse, ancient beyond any mason's memory of placing it.

A fossilized dragon egg resting alone in a cathedral-wide cave, far larger than the clutch eggs of the open hillsides, its shell fused to the cave floor by mineral accretion, the surface patterned with deep radial cracks never hatched through.

A dragon's scapula half-submerged in a bog, the blade of bone rising above the dark water like a collapsed sail, its glenoid socket hollow enough to shelter travelers from rain, scored deep with tendon-groove channels now filled with black peat.

A length of dragon vertebral column exposed by a landslide across the high pass, lying disarticulated over a quarter-mile of scree, each bone stamped on the underside with a crest-shaped process unlike any known creature's anatomy, the purpose wholly lost.

A colossal horned dragon skull half-buried nose-down in a hillside at a forty-degree angle, tall as a watchtower, its forward horn still intact and longer than a jousting lance, the eye socket wide enough to drive a cart through.

An immense ribcage arching over a mile of valley floor like a cathedral nave, each rib as thick as an ancient oak and pale as limestone, the highest arch lost in low cloud, grass growing thick between the fallen cross-bones below.

A complete dragon skeleton curled across an entire hillside as though the beast lay down to sleep and never rose, skull resting in the valley basin, tail tip vanishing into the treeline above, vertebrae each the size of a millstone.

A dragon spine running exposed through a cliff face for three hundred yards, the vertebrae locked in sedimentary rock like a seam of pale ore, each disc taller than a standing man, the column vanishing at both ends into unbroken stone.

A single wing's splayed bone-fingers and petrified membrane standing upright from the earth like a vast sail, the outermost finger-spar as long as a ship's mast, the membrane between turned to translucent grey stone that rings when wind strikes it.

A severed dragon talon thrust upright from a village common, each hooked toe-bone longer than a cottage rooftop, the knuckle joint still raised on a pedestal of fused earth scorched black beneath it by some ancient heat.

A dragon skeleton spanning a deep river gorge as a bone bridge, the spine and ribcage forming a natural walkway wide enough for a wagon, tail vertebrae anchored in the far cliff, the skull overhang providing a grim gatehouse above the void.

Three fossilized dragon eggs nested in a split granite hollow on an exposed ridgeline, each egg taller than a draft horse, their stone shells cracked but intact, the surface patterned with faint hexagonal scales pressed into the mineral from within.

A drift of shed dragon scales covering a whole meadow like enormous fallen leaves, each scale the width of a knight's shield and iridescent black-green, edges sharp enough to split boot leather, lying where some vast passage ended centuries ago.

A single dragon fang standing upright from a hilltop like a pale monolith, taller than a bell tower, slightly curved, its root still caked in the red iron-rich soil it erupted through, the tip worn to a blunt knob by a century of weather.

Claw gouges raked across an entire valley wall in four parallel trenches, each groove deep enough to shelter a man lying flat, the stone within the cuts vitrified to dark glass, the scratch-lines running three hundred feet before vanishing into collapse.

A whole dragon petrified mid-coil on a moorland plateau, turned entirely to dark basalt, the stone scales still individually defined, the outermost coil forming a wall taller than a fortified rampart, the blind stone eyes facing the eastern horizon.

A dragon tail's vertebrae trailing from a hillside bank into a lake, the last visible joint barely above the waterline, each bone pale and enormous, trailing into black water where local fishermen never lower nets and never explain why they refuse.

A dragon jawbone forming a natural arch over an old trade road, the lower jaw planted in both verges like a gate, teeth projecting downward from the arch above, the largest incisor missing, the gap long used as a lantern hook by travelers.

A ruined temple built around a massive dragon skull set upon a carved altar dais, the skull's cranium forming the sanctuary ceiling, collapsed nave walls leaning outward, moss filling every crack, the altar stone still scorched black at the center.

A toppled dragon-rider monument at a crossroads, the stone dragon base cracked and half-sunk, the rider statue snapped at the knee and lying face-down in the ditch, the dragon's carved neck still raised, a real dragon rib repurposed as the flagpole.

A barrow mound shaped unmistakably as a coiled dragon, the earthwork running the full length of a hillside, the head-mound crowned with slumped stones, the tail curving back on itself, the burial entrance passage framed by two genuine dragon ribs set upright.

A single dragon horn spiraling out of a hilltop at a steep angle like a pale ivory tower, twenty feet of its length exposed, the spiral groove running its length in a slow left-hand twist, the tip broken off and never found.

An ancient dragon nest of fused branches, bone, and river stone covering a depression as wide as an amphitheater, the woven rim walls still twelve feet high in places, the hollow interior worn smooth by centuries of rain pooling and draining away.

A mummified dragon wing draped over the broken wall of a collapsed fortress, the leathery membrane still largely intact and dark as old leather, the longest finger-spar resting on the far hillside, its tip submerged in a bog a quarter-mile away.

A dragon breastbone keel rising from a peat moor like a vast ship's prow, the sternum bone pale and enormous, standing taller than a manor house at its highest point, the attachment ridges for the great flight muscles still deeply pronounced along its flanks.

A ring of standing stones each carved from a different dragon skull, seventeen skulls in a rough circle on a windswept upland, the largest still horned and twice the height of a man, some tipped and cracked, others sunk to their eye sockets in the turf.

A fossilized dragon ribcage half-submerged in a coastal cliff face, the sea having carved the softer rock away around it, each exposed rib arching out over the beach below, the tide running through the lower ribs twice daily, the bone turned salt-grey and ringing hollow.

A single enormous dragon vertebra standing isolated on a river plain, taller than a two-story granary, its neural spine still intact, a shepherd's stone hut built into the hollow of its centrum, the doorframe formed by the natural arch of bone.

A collapsed dragon-skull gate where both halves of a split cranium flank an ancient road, each half resting at an outward lean, the interior braincase exposed and enormous, lichened walls of skull-bone rising on either side, the travelers' road passing between them like a gorge.
